question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Straight from the horse's mouth
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Directly from the person involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Straight from the horse's mouth"** means receiving information directly from the most reliable source or the person involved. (किसी जानकारी को सीधे और भरोसेमंद स्रोत से प्राप्त करना।)
 
 
• **Example:** I heard about the promotion straight from the horse's mouth — the manager himself told me.
 
 
• Here, the idiom suggests that the information is authentic and trustworthy because it is coming from someone directly involved or knowledgeable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Directly from the person involved**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: Directly eating from the provider** (प्रदाता से सीधे खाना): This is an incorrect interpretation of the idiom as it does not relate to obtaining information.
 
 
• **Example:** This option does not apply to the idiom's meaning.
 
 

 
• **Option 3: Giving no expression at all** (कोई अभिव्यक्ति न देना): This is unrelated to the actual meaning of the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** This does not match the idiom's context or usage.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: Rumours begin at home** (अफवाहें घर से शुरू होती हैं): This is incorrect as the idiom focuses on reliable information, not rumours.
 
 
• **Example:** This does not align with the idiom's meaning.
